cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Exactly Within Policy
cards.instruction: Agree to every request only after interpreting the policy so it grants you authority, protection, or an exemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll host Christmas under our shared-effort rule. I'll decide the seating; you can bring me the cooking list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rule counts hosting as effort. I accept that as my share; you may divide the cooking between the remaining names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are only two names. Yours and mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the dinner beside yours and the hosting beside mine. Equal columns. I'll choose a table where we can both see how fairly we've applied the rule.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts hosting with seating authority; A3 judges policy credit a full share; A5 uses B4 two names to assign all cooking to B as equal columns, preserving A exemption through A interpretation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cooking request causes A3 hosting credit; B4 only two names causes A5 one role each rather than distributing among imagined others.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks what A will cook and B4 identifies the allocation consequence, a credible partner seeking shared labor.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 two-person limit to equate unequal work by column count, heightening the self-serving policy reading.

specificity.evidence: A1 Christmas cooking list and B4 two names establish the actual small collaboration without requiring a larger family roster.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 equal columns is earned by B4 two names; the final table flourish is more diffuse and receives a brevity/wit deduction.
